title: Python Built-in Data Structures
intro: Python data structure interview questions for freshers almost always come down to one question the interviewer asks five different ways: 'do you know when to use each one?'. This page covers list (ordered, mutable, allows duplicates — the default workhorse), tuple (ordered, immutable — use when data should not change), dict (key-value pairs, O(1) lookup — the most important data structure in Python), and set (unordered, unique elements — use for membership tests and deduplication). It covers the comparison every interviewer asks (list vs tuple, dict vs set), list and dict comprehensions as the Pythonic way to build new collections from old ones, and the nested structure patterns that come up in JSON parsing. Every explanation starts with 'when would you reach for this one?' before the mechanics.
